title: The Architecture Needs a Door People Can Find
description: I am putting a public site in front of the work. The site is an entry point. It is not the knowledge platform.
body:
An architecture that can be read only by someone who already has the repository is not yet a public fact. Most people browse. They follow a door, a heading, a language they already speak. If the only way to understand VALESKA is to clone it, the work is still private even when the ideas are meant to travel.

Today I put a website in front of the work. Astro and TypeScript. A static build. Shared layout, navigation, footer. English and Dutch from the start, not as a retrofit. Placeholder pages and placeholder marks on purpose. A public face needs routes, language handling, and a repeatable build before it needs polish. The site is how the architecture can be explained. It is not the architecture.

The wrong default

The usual product site pretends the platform is already a finished service. Screenshots of a future. Claims the repository has not earned. I am not doing that. The first pages are placeholders because the substance still lives in the design documents and the working index. The public layer has to tell the truth about that: here is the purpose, here is the evidence, here is what is not yet built.

A shop window is not the workshop. It should not be empty, and it should not display goods that are still on the bench. Structure before ornament. That is the same rule as the knowledge layer: identity and a place to stand before interpretation.

A small operational decision

npm failed in this environment with an SSL cipher error. I did not paper over it. I moved the install to pnpm, wrote down the rationale, the test errors, and the phase status, and the build succeeded. That is a modest incident. It is also the same discipline VALESKA asks of everything else: an operational choice should be visible. A green build matters. The path that makes it reproducible matters too.

Internationalization is in the foundation. Dutch is in the first commit because a later retrofit is how language becomes a costume. The knowledge platform will need Spanish and Portuguese in other work. This site, on this date, is English and Dutch, static, local-first.

The committed assets are honest about their status: a logo placeholder, a favicon placeholder, an image for sharing, a whitepaper stand-in. Forms that would write leads are sketched for a later Cloudflare step. None of that is the index. None of that should be described as a running petroleum-governance product. The door is real. The goods in the window are still labeled as not yet made. A static site that tells the truth is already more of a public face than a handsome page that implies a service nobody can log into.

What this is not

The website is not a content store. It does not hold the index. It does not replace Alfresco, a file share, or the MCP tools. The next work is to replace placeholders with material that shows how VALESKA connects knowledge, process, and evidence without asking an organization to abandon the systems where the records already live.

Historical basis: VALESKA commit c260f5f, December 25, 2025; contemporaneous website Phase 1 and Phase 2 status notes, pnpm rationale, and the Astro project under docs/Guyana Valeska/Web Presence/valeska-website/. Phase status files are dated December 24; the commit timestamp is the publication-date authority.
